stem: During prospective legal review, a pharmacy pours controlled tablets into ordinary trash after removing patient labels. Why is this insufficient?

choices.text: Removing patient labels makes the tablets non-retrievable.
Ordinary trash is acceptable after an employee witnesses disposal.
Crushing the tablets without mixing or chemical alteration is always sufficient.
Use the sewer whenever the product appears on an FDA flush list.
Registrant destruction must render the controlled substances permanently non-retrievable.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Registrant destruction must render the controlled substances permanently non-retrievable.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Removing patient labels makes the tablets non-retrievable.' would require that privacy de-identification altered the drug's physical or chemical condition. The decisive cue appears in 'During prospective legal review, a pharmacy pours controlled tablets into ordinary trash after removing patient labels. Why is this insufficient?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Removing patient labels makes the tablets non-retrievable.' would apply only if privacy de-identification altered the drug's physical or chemical condition; 'During prospective legal review, a pharmacy pours controlled tablets into ordinary trash after removing patient labels. Why is this insufficient?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Ordinary trash is acceptable after an employee witnesses disposal.' would apply only if witnessing alone met the destruction standard; 'During prospective legal review, a pharmacy pours controlled tablets into ordinary trash after removing patient labels. Why is this insufficient?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Crushing the tablets without mixing or chemical alteration is always sufficient.' would apply only if crushing alone necessarily made recovery and practical use impossible; 'During prospective legal review, a pharmacy pours controlled tablets into ordinary trash after removing patient labels. Why is this insufficient?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Use the sewer whenever the product appears on an FDA flush list.' would apply only if ultimate-user disposal guidance governed registrant destruction methods; 'During prospective legal review, a pharmacy pours controlled tablets into ordinary trash after removing patient labels. Why is this insufficient?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Registrant destruction must render the controlled substances permanently non-retrievable.': supported by destruction standard.

related_facts: Controlled substances destroyed by a registrant must be rendered non-retrievable so their physical or chemical condition is permanently altered and unavailable for practical use.
explanation.mpje_trap: 'Removing patient labels makes the tablets non-retrievable.' would apply if privacy de-identification altered the drug's physical or chemical condition. In 'During prospective legal review, a pharmacy pours controlled tablets into ordinary trash after removing patient labels. Why is this insufficient?', that predicate is missing.

reasoning_steps: Match the scenario's operative facts to Non-retrievable standard for controlled-substance destruction
Reject nearby rules whose schedule, trigger, deadline, or actor differs from Destruction standard
